# PLAN — iteration 4
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 7 LUTs and 9 FFs, so this iteration must strictly reduce LUTs to improve the objective. The three prior candidates were rejected: natural 8-bit increment increased LUTs, the equivalent terminal-count comparison left LUTs unchanged, and the nibble comparator increased LUTs. The source’s 32-bit counter only visits 0–255 after reset; its numeric top latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the increment-and-clear structure with explicit bit-toggle equations for the modulo-256 counter may reduce counter next-state logic while preserving the registered PWM behavior.

## Instruction for generator
Keep the synchronous reset and registered `pwm_out` comparison unchanged. Replace the counter’s `counter == 255` clear branch and `counter + 1` update with bitwise toggle equations for `counter[7:0]`: bit 0 toggles every cycle, and each higher bit toggles when all lower bits are 1; keep `counter[31:8]` zero on each nonreset cycle. This implements modulo-256 counting from the reset state; retain the exact observable cycles and accept the candidate only if the unchanged simulation, routed metric integrity, setup and hold gates pass and LUT usage strictly improves over the incumbent.
